prompts.title: Recent Form — Kinetic Result Words vs Grouped Count Bars
prompts.prompt: Vertical 9:16 stage on GoatLab charcoal #101412 with a permanent yellow subtitle band occupying the lower quarter; all composition lives in the upper three quarters. Editorial variant first: kinetic typography. The heading 'FORMA RECIENTE' in condensed warm white #edf0e6 caps snaps into the top third, then the Spanish words 'VICTORIAS', 'EMPATES', 'DERROTAS' cascade one per narration beat, stamped alternately in lime #c5ed74 for Arsenal FC and slate #8ca6bf for Everton FC, with a rhythmic scale-pulse on every beat. No axes, no counts, no sample claims and no invented match events — only the two team names and three result words, hard-cut with a subtle camera push-in. Exit: the words collapse into a single lime line that wipes upward. Statistical variant: grouped count bars on a shared zero baseline. Two clusters — 'Arsenal FC' left, 'Everton FC' right — each with three vertical bars for victorias, empates and derrotas; heights bind to {{home.wins}}, {{home.draws}} and {{home.losses}} for Arsenal FC and {{away.wins}}, {{away.draws}} and {{away.losses}} for Everton FC, all in the unit 'partidos' on one common scale so the six bars are directly comparable. Bars grow from the baseline across roughly one second, Arsenal in lime, Everton in slate, warm white tabular numerals above each bar, Spanish category labels beneath the clusters. A caption under the chart reads 'Últimos {{home.n}} partidos (Arsenal FC) · {{away.n}} partidos (Everton FC)' and doubles as the sample statement, with the source note 'Fuente: Bzzoiro' at the chart foot; stating both samples explicitly lets viewers judge comparability. Emphasis: a lime highlight holds on the strongest cluster while the rest dims slightly. Camera: slow vertical drift, no rotation. The transition in and the transition out are charcoal luma wipes timed to the narration; the subtitle band never moves.

prompts.title: Goals For and Against — Ball Paths vs Paired Bars
prompts.prompt: Vertical 9:16 frame, charcoal #101412 base, yellow subtitle band fixed across the lower quarter. Editorial variant: an illustrative football pitch drawn top-down in thin warm white #edf0e6 strokes fills the upper three quarters, with the Spanish heading 'GOLES' in condensed caps. A lime #c5ed74 ball enters from the bottom and traces a curved path toward the top goal, leaving a glowing trail; a second slate #8ca6bf ball mirrors it from the opposite side, so the two paths visually duel without any scoreboard, numbers or invented match events. Camera performs a slow top-down drift following the balls; trails fade and pitch lines retract to exit. Statistical variant: the pitch dissolves into a paired bar chart. Two team columns — 'Arsenal FC' left, 'Everton FC' right — each holding two vertical bars on one shared scale measured in 'goles': 'GOLES A FAVOR' and 'GOLES RECIBIDOS'. Heights bind to {{home.gf}} and {{home.ga}} for Arsenal FC and to {{away.gf}} and {{away.ga}} for Everton FC; identical axis bounds keep the four bars mutually comparable, and the Spanish axis caption 'goles' sits at the baseline. Bars rise from the zero line in a staggered one-second cascade, Arsenal in lime, Everton in slate, warm white tabular numerals above each bar. Emphasis lands on the tallest bar with a brief lime pulse while the others hold. Under the chart, a caption reads 'Últimos {{home.n}} y {{away.n}} partidos' with the source line 'Fuente: Bzzoiro', so the sample behind every figure stays visible. Football context persists as a faint pitch watermark behind the bars. Transition in: a diagonal charcoal wipe from the editorial pitch; transition out: a downward push that hands off to the next block. One focal point: the four-bar pair.

prompts.title: Clean Sheets — Shield Energy vs Count Bars with Samples
prompts.prompt: Vertical 9:16 composition on charcoal #101412 with the yellow subtitle band locked across the lower quarter. Editorial variant: defensive energy sequence. Two stylised shields rise from the bottom of the upper three quarters — a lime #c5ed74 shield for Arsenal FC on the left, a slate #8ca6bf shield for Everton FC on the right — each built from layered geometric plates that assemble with a metallic snap. Pulsing energy rings emanate from each shield in its team colour while the Spanish heading 'ARCOS EN CERO' stamps in above in warm white #edf0e6 condensed caps. The shields brace against an invisible impact, plates flexing, then settle; no numbers, no axes, no sample claims, no invented match events. Camera: slow push-in toward the midpoint where the shields nearly touch. Exit: both shields dissolve into particles that drift upward. Statistical variant: the particles re-form into two horizontal count bars on a shared zero baseline at the left edge, one per team, labelled 'Arsenal FC' and 'Everton FC', lengths bound to {{home.clean}} and {{away.clean}} in the unit 'partidos', with warm white numerals at each bar end. Directly beneath each bar a smaller slate caption anchors the sample: 'en {{home.n}} partidos' and 'en {{away.n}} partidos', so the counts are always read together with their sample size and never converted into rates or ratios of any kind. A source line 'Fuente: Bzzoiro' sits at the chart foot. Bars extend left-to-right in a firm one-second ease; emphasis holds on the longer bar with a lime edge glow while the Spanish captions stay legible. Transition in: particle convergence from the editorial shields; transition out: a clean vertical wipe. Keep one focal point — the bar pair — with everything else subdued.

prompts.title: Head-to-Head — Colour Duel vs Stacked Historical Bar
prompts.prompt: Vertical 9:16 stage, charcoal #101412 ground, permanent yellow subtitle band across the lower quarter. Editorial variant: a visual duel. The upper three quarters split along a jagged diagonal — lime #c5ed74 territory for Arsenal FC above-left, slate #8ca6bf territory for Everton FC below-right — with the Spanish heading 'ENFRENTAMIENTOS DIRECTOS' in warm white #edf0e6 condensed caps striking across the seam. The two colour fields slide toward each other, compress into a single clash line that vibrates on the narration beat, then recoil to their halves; a thin warm white spark travels the seam. No counts, no axes, no sample claims, no invented match events. Camera: slow lateral dolly following the compression. Exit: the seam flashes and both fields slide off opposite edges. Statistical variant: the seam becomes a single horizontal stacked bar spanning the full width, total length bound to {{h2h.total}} matches ('partidos'), segmented into three parts on one shared scale: a lime segment for 'VICTORIAS ARSENAL FC' bound to {{h2h.homeWins}}, a warm white segment for 'EMPATES' bound to {{h2h.draws}}, and a slate segment for 'VICTORIAS EVERTON FC' bound to {{h2h.awayWins}}. Segments extend sequentially from the left over about two seconds, each with its Spanish label and warm white numeral; a header line reads 'CRUCES PREVIOS: {{h2h.total}} partidos'. A source note 'Fuente: Bzzoiro' anchors the chart foot, and a slate disclaimer states 'Historial · no es un pronóstico', making explicit that this sample describes history only and is not a forecast. Emphasis: the lime segment pulses once as the narration names Arsenal FC. Transition in: the editorial clash line morphs into the bar's baseline; transition out: segments retract right-to-left. The stacked bar remains the single focal point.

prompts.title: Synthesis — Attack Meets Defence
prompts.prompt: Vertical 9:16 frame on charcoal #101412, yellow subtitle band fixed across the lower quarter. Editorial variant: team reveals with narrative emphasis. First Arsenal FC reveals — the name sets in warm white #edf0e6 condensed caps across the upper third while a lime #c5ed74 light sweep passes behind it; then Everton FC reveals lower, backed by a slate #8ca6bf sweep. Between them a thin vertical seam of light thins and vibrates, staging the tension; the Spanish heading 'ATAQUE CONTRA DEFENSA' stamps in last with a single rhythmic pulse. No numbers, no axes, no sample claims, no invented match events. Camera: slow converging push toward the seam. Exit: the seam snaps and both names slide to opposite edges. Statistical variant: two stacked stat cards replace the names, deliberately not on a shared axis because their units differ. Card one, lime-edged: label 'GOLES A FAVOR · ARSENAL FC', figure bound to {{home.gf}} in the unit 'goles', caption 'en {{home.n}} partidos'. Card two, slate-edged: label 'ARCOS EN CERO · EVERTON FC', figure bound to {{away.clean}} in the unit 'partidos', caption 'en {{away.n}} partidos'. Cards slide in from opposite sides over one second each, warm white tabular numerals, Spanish labels above each figure. A source line 'Fuente: Bzzoiro' sits beneath the cards, and a slate tag reads 'historial reciente', distinguishing these history figures from any estimate — no model estimates appear because none are published. Emphasis: a soft glow alternates between cards as the narration weighs attack against defence, ending on the defensive card. Transition in: the editorial seam morphs into the gap between cards; transition out: cards fade to charcoal. One focal point at a time, hierarchy kept by size.
